items.title: FBI Agents Visit Anti-ICE Protester: "Your name was brought up."
items.raw_content: While the media continues to ignore and even mock Trump’s war on “Antifa” terrorism as legally impossible, the FBI is quietly interrogating protesters. The Bureau is targeting anti-ICE protesters not charged with any crime, like Chicago-based English professor Elias Cepeda, as I recently reported . Often people targeted have refused to go public with their experience, fearing retribution. But one protester, fed up with the culture of self-censorship, decided to share his story. His account sheds light on the FBI’s attempts to map out some organized Antifa superstructure — and in doing so, undermining Americans’ freedom of speech and political expression.
items.title_zh: FBI探员造访反ICE抗议者：“有人提到了你的名字”
items.summary: The article reports that FBI agents have visited anti-ICE protesters who have not been charged with crimes, including a Chicago English professor, as part of what it describes as an effort to map an “Antifa” structure. One protester described the experience publicly despite fearing retribution.

items.title: New OSM file format: 30% smaller than PBF, 5x faster to import
items.raw_content: The OSM dataset is huge, and keeps growing every day. Great news, of course, but sometimes the sheer volume can be overwhelming – there are just gobs and gobs of data! Hence, we created GOB (“Geo-Object Bundle”), a new file format that makes tackling OSM data faster and easier. It’s a companion format to our now-familiar Geo-Object Library (essentially, a tightly-compressed GOL with its indexes stripped). To support this new format, GOL Tool 2.1 has two new commands: save GOLs as GOBs and load ...
items.title_zh: OpenStreetMap新文件格式：比PBF小30%、导入快5倍
items.summary: A new OpenStreetMap file format called GOB (Geo-Object Bundle) is a companion to the Geo-Object Library format, essentially a tightly compressed GOL with its indexes stripped, and GOL Tool 2.1 adds commands to save GOLs as GOBs and load them.
